subject: International payment: fee allocation and currency options
messages:
From: Julien Moreau <julien.moreau@acme-corp.fr>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 12:15:00 +0200
Subject: Payment for INV-5892 / bank details and fee handling

Hi Aisha,

We received invoice INV-5892 for the May usage. Our AP team needs final bank instructions and a quick confirmation on how intermediary bank fees should be handled. We generally send EUR payments from our French treasury but our UK procurement prefers GBP for consolidation — both could be possible. A few specific questions: 

- Can Redwood accept an EUR payment (SEPA or SWIFT) and credit it net of correspondent fees, or do you require OUR to ensure we cover intermediaries?
- If we wire from our UK treasury in GBP, do you have a GBP nostro at a UK bank and what is the exact beneficiary name/account to avoid matching delays?
- Any VAT handling notes we should include on the remittance to help with our reclaim process?

Attached a proposed settlement schedule and our invoice reference. Please advise so we can process before month-end.

Thanks,
Julien
Julien Moreau
Head of Treasury, Acme Corp
Attachments: AP_schedule_May.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Julien Moreau <julien.moreau@acme-corp.fr>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 15:03:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Payment for INV-5892 / bank details and fee handling

Hi Julien — thanks for the clear note. Below are the options and our recommended approach depending on which treasury you choose to pay from. Short version: we can accept both EUR and GBP; the only difference is how you handle intermediary charges.

Option A — EUR (preferred for EU payers, SEPA where possible):
- SEPA (preferred): use our EUR account in NL (IBAN NL... / BIC...). No intermediary. Please include invoice number INV-5892 in the remittance reference.
- SWIFT EUR: if you send via SWIFT, choose SHA (shared) if your bank insists; we will reconcile but may receive a lower net amount if correspondent banks deduct fees. If you want to guarantee full invoiced amount, use OUR.

Option B — GBP (from UK treasury):
- We accept GBP into our sterling account with Barclays UK (Account name: Redwood Inference Inc (Eurasia), Sort Code: 20-XX-XX, Account: 12345678). Use the full beneficiary name exactly as above.
- When wiring GBP, intermediary/correspondent fees are rare but possible if routing crosses non-GBP rails. Again, OUR guarantees the full amount.

Fee allocation guidance: 
- SHA (shared) = each side pays their own bank fees; Redwood will reconcile on receipt and may request shortfall if net < invoice.
- OUR = payer covers all intermediaries and beneficiary receives full gross amount.
- If Acme prefers to keep SHA, please add 1.8% contingency on the wire to cover potential correspondent deductions (this is advisory; we will follow up if shortfall occurs).

VAT / remittance reference: 
- Please include: INV-5892, Acme Corp VAT FR123456789, and the invoice period (Apr 2027). That helps our finance team populate the VAT fields for EU reclaim.

I am attaching a short payment-instructions text file and our invoice PDF for your AP. If you confirm which treasury (EUR or GBP) and whether you will send OUR vs SHA, we will confirm the exact account/beneficiary string and next steps.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_payment_instructions.txt, INV-5892.pdf

We'll attach the wire instruction to the payment. If you recommend we do OUR to avoid reconciliation, let us know the premium.

Best,
